diagnostic_metadata.element_inspected: Reinforced Concrete Shear Wall (Bay 4, Elevation +18.5 ft)
diagnostic_metadata.code_standard: ACI 224R-01: Control of Cracking in Concrete Structures

possible_causes: Diagonal tension shear stress exceeding concrete tensile capacity under localized load redistribution
Minor differential settlement of adjacent pile cap foundation footing
Restrained thermal contraction coupled with high curing heat differential during initial concrete pour
engineering_analysis.structural_risk_assessment: The diagonal angle (~45 degrees) and aperture width (> 1.5 mm) indicate active shear stress transfer. Rebar bond slip or yield may be occurring if loading is dynamic.
recommended_next_steps: Step 1: Install dual calibrated mechanical crack tell-tale monitoring gauges across the fissure to track active movement over 14 days.
Step 2: Commission a formal physical site inspection by a licensed Structural Engineer of Record (SEOR).
Step 3: Conduct non-destructive Ultrasonic Pulse Velocity (UPV) or rebound hammer testing to evaluate depth of penetration.
Step 4: If active movement ceases, execute low-viscosity epoxy resin pressure injection to restore monolithic shear resistance and prevent rebar carbonation/corrosion.

disclaimer: ENGINEERING DISCLAIMER: Image-based crack diagnostics are preliminary AI estimates intended for initial triage only. This output cannot replace a formal physical and structural inspection by a licensed Professional Engineer (PE) or qualified structural consultant.
